title: Ad fatigue, solved in minutes with the Agentic Marketing Platform
summary: Use agents to monitor your entire ad program for fatiguing ads and automatically create new ad variants.
body_markdown:
Every ad fatigues eventually. The question is how much you spend before you replace it.


With targeting increasingly automated, creative is what separates a winning campaign from wasted spend. But refreshing creative is still a manual, multi-team process. Someone has to spot the fatigue, write the brief, and wait on creative, which means most teams only catch it on their highest-spend ads. Everywhere else, it’s death by a thousand cuts.


This is exactly the kind of repetitive, time-sensitive work agents are good at accelerating. With the Hightouch Agentic Marketing Platform, agents watch every ad, write the refresh brief, and build new variations from your approved assets, all in one, fast agentic workflow. All you have to do is review what they made and launch it. A process that used to take a week or more now takes a few minutes.


## The process today: marketers have to choose between speed and quality


Solving creative ad fatigue comes down to two things:


1. **Speed.** The faster you can launch new ads to replace old ones, the better your performance will be. Every day a fatigued ad stays live, you pay more for worse results.
2. **Creative diversity:** It’s not enough to just change the text in a refreshed ad. Ad platforms reward new layouts, treatments, and formats, so a refresh needs real variety.


In a manual process, those two things are trade-offs. If you want to move fast, you don’t get as much variety. If you want variety, you can’t move fast.


Today, the process takes days or weeks and looks something like this:


1. **Monitor:** Performance lead checks ad performance in the different ad platforms and identifies which ads need a refresh. They decide which ones to prioritize. In practice, that means the highest-spend campaigns are closely monitored.
2. **Brief:** Manually pull together the original ads, approved images, and copy. Submit a brief to creative for new versions and explain what can and can’t change.
3. **Build:** Creative adds them to the queue. Depending on in-flight projects, this can be a few days to two weeks.
4. **Review:** Get the updated assets back and route them for approval.
5. **Launch:** Days later, launch the ads.


That’s five handoffs across at least two teams, and a week or more before fresh ads goes live.


## The new way: agents speed up


Instead of treating performance monitoring and creative production as separate jobs and handing off work between them, the team sets up an agentic workflow that connects them.


1. **Monitor:** An agent checks every ad across your connected platforms against your fatigue thresholds and flags the ones wearing out, categorizing ads by highest impact based on spend.
2. **Brief:** An agent writes the refresh brief: what to keep, what to change, which approved images to use, and how many variants to build.
3. **Build:** An agent creates new variations of every fatigued ad using approved layouts and images.
4. **Review:** The agent pings the assigned reviewer for review in Slack.
5. **Launch:** The marketer reviews, makes edits, and launches.


Those first four steps all happen in about 6 minutes. Instead of waiting to refresh creative and seeing performance dip, you can launch refreshed ads the same day you learn about fatigue.


Respond to creative fatigue fast and launch new ads directly from Hightouch.
